Based on my chemical knowledge, I need to analyze this question carefully:

When esters react with alkali metals (like sodium or lithium) or metal hydrides (like sodium hydride or lithium aluminum hydride), the reaction involves reduction of the ester. In these reactions, the metal or metal hydride acts as a source of hydride ions (H⁻) which attack the carbonyl carbon of the ester.

During this reaction, the hydrogen from the metal hydride replaces the alkoxy group (-OR) of the ester. The displaced alkoxy group takes a proton from the solvent (often an alcohol), and in this process, hydrogen gas (H₂) is released.

For example, when an ester reacts with lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH₄), the ester is reduced to an alcohol, and hydrogen gas is evolved.

Similarly, when an ester reacts with alkali metals like sodium, the metal donates electrons to the carbonyl group, and hydrogen gas is produced as a byproduct.

Therefore, the gas released when esters react with alkali metals and hydrides is hydrogen.
